name: ToastContent
description: The content layout (self-start, title-only sizing, body centering) needs to know which parts actually rendered. That used to be an ancestor `:has()` styling descendants — a whole-page recalculation trap in Chromium (#386). It measures the rendered DOM after layout instead, so wrapped parts and parts that render nothing behave exactly like the old selectors did.

props.name: sticky

props.name: actionTimeout
props.description: How long a toast from the `toast` command API stays when it has an action or is an `error`, in ms. Defaults to 8000, or to `timeout` when that is longer, and to 0 when `timeout` is 0.

props.name: limit
props.description: The maximum number of toasts that can be displayed at once. When the limit is exceeded, the oldest toasts are marked as `limited` (via the `data-limited` attribute) rather than removed, so they can be hidden or animated out.

props.name: timeout
props.description: The default amount of time (in ms) before a toast is auto dismissed. A value of `0` will prevent the toast from being dismissed automatically.

props.name: toastManager
props.description: A global manager for toasts to use outside of a React component.

name: ToastRoot
description: A toast pushed past the provider's `limit` by a newer one is closed, not held back: toasts replace each other and never queue, so an older toast can't come back when the newer one goes. Its swipe direction follows the viewport's edge unless `swipeDirection` is passed.
